title: Reduce-then-evaluate: dist O M = dist O N for MechMath IMO 2026 Q2
intent: Prove the competition goal `dist O M = dist O N` by reducing it, through a normalisation lemma, to an equivalent statement in normalised complex coordinates, then closing that statement with two algebra lemmas chained through a real-part identity, and pulling the result back through the iff.
also_known_as: reduce to a normal form and close

parent.name: main_theorem
parent.statement:
theorem main_theorem
    (A B C K L O : Plane)
    -- `ABC` is a nondegenerate triangle.
    (hABC : ¬ Collinear ℝ ({A, B, C} : Set Plane))
    -- `M`, `N` are the midpoints of `AB`, `AC`.
    (M N : Plane) (hM : M = midpoint ℝ A B) (hN : N = midpoint ℝ A C)
    -- `K` is inside triangle `BMC`; `L` is inside triangle `BNC`.
    (hK : InsideTriangle B M C K)
    (hL : InsideTriangle B N C L)
    -- `K` inside angle `∠ L B A`; `L` inside angle `∠ A C K`.
    (hKangle : InsideAngle L B A K)
    (hLangle : InsideAngle A C K L)
    -- The three angle equalities.
    (h1 : ∠ K B A = ∠ A C L)
    (h2 : ∠ L B K = ∠ L N C)
    (h3 : ∠ L C K = ∠ B M K)
    -- `O` is the circumcentre of triangle `AKL`.
    (hO : IsCircumcentre A K L O) :
    dist O M = dist O N

children.name: normalized_reduction
children.statement:
theorem normalized_reduction
    (A B C K L O : Plane)
    (hABC : ¬ Collinear ℝ ({A, B, C} : Set Plane))
    (M N : Plane) (hM : M = midpoint ℝ A B) (hN : N = midpoint ℝ A C)
    (hK : InsideTriangle B M C K)
    (hL : InsideTriangle B N C L)
    (hKangle : InsideAngle L B A K)
    (hLangle : InsideAngle A C K L)
    (h1 : ∠ K B A = ∠ A C L)
    (h2 : ∠ L B K = ∠ L N C)
    (h3 : ∠ L C K = ∠ B M K)
    (hO : IsCircumcentre A K L O) :
    ∃ c k l o : ℂ,
      (2 * (starRingEnd ℂ o * k).re = Complex.normSq k)
    ∧ (2 * (starRingEnd ℂ o * l).re = Complex.normSq l)
    ∧ (starRingEnd ℂ k * l).im ≠ 0
    ∧ (2 * ((starRingEnd ℂ (c - 1) * l).im) * Complex.normSq k
        + 2 * ((starRingEnd ℂ k * (c - 1)).im) * Complex.normSq l
        - (Complex.normSq c - 1) * (starRingEnd ℂ k * l).im = 0)
    ∧ (dist O M = dist O N ↔ dist o (1/2 : ℂ) = dist o (c/2))
children.closed_by: exact ⟨c, k, l, o, hOk, hOl, hΔ, hC, hiff⟩
children.note: Reduces the configuration to normalised complex coordinates (A ↦ 0, B ↦ 1, M ↦ 1/2, N ↦ c/2) and returns four facts plus the iff `dist O M = dist O N ↔ dist o (1/2) = dist o (c/2)`. It closes on its own by chaining named siblings: re_of_norm_eq (hOk, hOl), coeff_match + akl_noncollinear (hΔ), and certificate_from_angles (hC).

children.name: circumcenter_determinant
children.statement:
theorem circumcenter_determinant
    (c k l o : ℂ)
    (hΔ : (starRingEnd ℂ k * l).im ≠ 0)
    (hC : 2 * ((starRingEnd ℂ (c-1) * l).im) * Complex.normSq k
        + 2 * ((starRingEnd ℂ k * (c-1)).im) * Complex.normSq l
        - (Complex.normSq c - 1) * (starRingEnd ℂ k * l).im = 0)
    (hOk : 2 * (starRingEnd ℂ o * k).re = Complex.normSq k)
    (hOl : 2 * (starRingEnd ℂ o * l).re = Complex.normSq l) :
    2 * (starRingEnd ℂ o * (c-1)).re = (Complex.normSq c - 1) / 2
children.note: From the circumcentre equations (hOk, hOl), the certificate (hC) and the nonvanishing determinant Δ ≠ 0, derives the real-part identity hF1 by a linear_combination of hC, hOk, hOl and then cancels Δ.

children.name: distance_bridge
children.statement:
theorem distance_bridge (c o : ℂ)
    (hF1 : 2 * (starRingEnd ℂ o * (c - 1)).re = (Complex.normSq c - 1) / 2) :
    dist o (1/2 : ℂ) = dist o (c/2)
children.note: Turns the real-part identity hF1 into the normalised distance equality `dist o (1/2) = dist o (c/2)` by expanding both sides to Complex.normSq and closing with nlinarith.

applicability.goal_shape: An equality between two distances (more generally, a geometric predicate) that becomes a simple algebraic identity after an explicit coordinate normalisation: here `dist O M = dist O N` normalises to `dist o (1/2) = dist o (c/2)` by mapping the plane to ℂ with B ↦ 1 and A ↦ 0.
applicability.use_when: the geometry admits an isometry into coordinates (here `g : Plane ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] ℂ`), the normalisation returns an iff so the reduced goal is equivalent, and each step of the evaluation (the certificate, the determinant identity, the distance bridge) can be stated as its own named lemma whose hypotheses the reduction supplies exactly.
applicability.avoid_when: the reduction is only one direction (the pull-back needs an iff, or at least a suffices direction); the normalisation itself carries most of the difficulty, so the reduction lemma is really the theorem rather than a leaf; or the reduced algebra statement still needs a certificate too large to state and prove as its own lemma.
